chapter: Judgments on Ellington, Parker and others
title: Johnny Wiggs and his pupils
summary: Rose calls Johnny Wiggs the most competent musician he knew. They note his pupils Charlie DeVore, Pete Fountain, Jack Delaney and George Girard, and that he worked in New York vaudeville bands.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: And, okay, what... Let me just ask you this before we close because we're getting close. Who have you closely worked with that you've particularly been impressed by?
Oh, Johnny Wiggs. I consider Johnny Wiggs to be the most competent musician I ever knew.
Nobody knows who Johnny Wiggs is.
But I might mention that Johnny Wiggs was the teacher of Charlie DeVore.
And also of Pete Fountain, Jack Delaney, George Gerard. But for me,
Charlie DeVore is a particular interest because he plays in the Hall Brothers Band in Mendota.
And so it makes a connection to my home territory. But he was also a teacher of Pete Fountain.
And he's a New Orleans based person. He never left New Orleans?
For any extended period of time?
Oh, yes, yes. He certainly did. He worked in New York. He worked in Vaudeville bands.
